remarks_1999: Whitney Archive indicates, "Exam. at Amer. Place, March 1946 [notes inscription 2]. . . . Note: Georgia O'Keeffe calls this 'Black Iris.' Small purple iris with green stem." O'Keeffe wrote: "For several years I looked for the black iris at the time it should bloom. I could only find it in New York flower shops for about two weeks in the spring and I painted it many times –– year after year" (*Georgia O'Keeffe* [1976], unpaginated, text accompanying entry 30). (Source: Lynes, 1999)

description: A dark purple and gray iris, supported by a dark green stem, fills the composition. The background of the composition is textured like a crumpled piece of paper and rendered in tones of bluish gray.
